title: Is "fish" even a thing?
question: Why do biologists say "fish" is not one tidy group?
hook: Your own ancestors were fish, which makes the word surprisingly hard to define.
idea: Since four-limbed land vertebrates descend from fish, "fish" covers every vertebrate except them and is a handy label, not a complete branch of the family tree.

beats.prompt: Imagine one branch of the family tree that holds the earliest fish and every one of their descendants. Where would humans sit?

choices.label: Outside it, because our ancestors left the water long ago
choices.feedback: Leaving the water does not remove a lineage from its ancestry: tetrapods still descend from fish.

choices.label: On a separate branch, because we breathe with lungs
choices.feedback: It tempts because lungs seem new, but tetrapod lungs are homologous to swim bladders, which fish already had.

choices.label: Inside it, because tetrapods descend from fish

beats.explain: Tetrapods, including humans, are modified bony fishes. A branch holding every descendant of the first fish would include us, and "fish" would match "vertebrates".

beats.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
pairs: Ray-finned fish that can protrude their jaws
Four-limbed vertebrates, mostly living on land
beats.explain: Each term names a piece of the fish story, from the science itself to the land vertebrates that grew out of it.

beats.prompt: Add up every living species of amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals. How does that total compare with living fish species?

choices.label: The four land-linked classes together are far larger
choices.feedback: Mammals and birds get the attention, but they are small groups next to fish.

choices.label: Fish alone outnumber all four classes combined
The two totals are roughly equal
choices.feedback: Fish are not close to a tie: with over 33,000 species they pass the other four classes combined.

beats.explain: With over 33,000 living species, fish are easily the largest group of vertebrates, more than the other four traditional classes combined.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Four-limbed land vertebrates evolved from lobe-finned fish.
So any group containing all jawed fish must also contain those land vertebrates.
So fish, leaving them out, form a paraphyletic group.
That is why Pisces is still the standard formal class for fish.
beats.explain: Because fish without tetrapods are paraphyletic, the class Pisces from older reference works is no longer used in formal classifications.
